name: Massachusetts
summary: Statutes: malegislature.gov General Laws (unofficial) are constructible from chapter and section alone, because /Laws/GeneralLaws/Chapter{c}/Section{s} redirects to the Part/Title URL. A public JSON API (/api/Chapters/{c}/Sections/{s}) returns the same text, and Justia 2025 is the tier-2 fallback. The Constitution is a single 357K-character page that WebFetch cannot read past the early Amendments; fetch_doc.py reads all of it. Court rules and the Guide to Evidence have per-rule pages on mass.gov (index-anchored slugs that drop the decimal point) plus full-set PDFs (corpus candidates). CMR chapters are mass.gov PDFs (unofficial), with LII as a constructible tier-2 source. Case law: mass.gov carries only recent slip opinions; 128archive.com (Reporter of Decisions) has a GET search of Rule 23.0 decisions since 2008; Justia is the free route for older opinions. No free official Mass. Reports pagination exists. The FAR docket host (ma-appellatecourts.org) refuses automated access.

citation_map.notes: Massachusetts style (SJC Style Manual) cites 'G. L. c. 93A, § 9', 'St. 2016, c. 219, § 35', 'art. 14 of the Massachusetts Declaration of Rights' / 'art. 89 of the Amendments' (Arabic numerals; the legislature's anchors use Roman), 'Mass. R. Civ. P. 12 (b) (6)' (space before subdivision parentheses), 'Mass. G. Evid. § 803(6)(A)', '940 CMR 3.16'. Bluebook: 'Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 93A, § 9', 'Mass. Const. pt. 1, art. 14', 'Mass. Const. amend. art. 89', '940 Mass. Code Regs. 3.16'. ALM GL is the LexisNexis annotated code. No public-domain citation; Mass. and Mass. App. Ct. are official (LexisNexis), N.E. is West. Rule 23.0 (formerly 1:28) summary decisions are cited by case name, the Mass. App. Ct. table page where noted (pages 1101+), and a Rule 23.0 / 1:28 notation; those issued before Feb. 26, 2008 may not be cited. FAR is cited 'further appellate review denied, 491 Mass. 1102 (2023)' (table pages 1101+). Routing guards: bare 'c. 93A' or 'chapter 93A' without G.L./General Laws, bare 'Rule 12', bare 'Declaration of Rights' (also Maryland, New Hampshire) and bare 'N.E.2d/3d' (also IL, IN, NY, OH) must not route here without a Massachusetts marker; the N.E. regex requires a '(Mass.' or '(Mass. App. Ct.' parenthetical. 'Mass. App. Div.' and 'Mass. App. Dec.' (District Court Appellate Division) are excluded from the case regex. Docket numbers: SJC-NNNNN, FAR-NNNNN, YY-P-NNNN (panel) and YY-J-NNNN (single justice); route on dockets only with Massachusetts context. Section ranges '§§ 60B-60E' are spans: the regex takes the first section (MA section numbers never contain hyphens). law_aliases maps popular names to chapter/section from memory (unverified) and rule abbreviations to source ids. CourtListener ids from memory, unverified. Fixes 2026-10-16 (independent check): the constitution regex now also matches 'art. N of the Declaration of Rights of the Massachusetts Constitution', and the CMR regex matches the Bluebook form '940 Mass. Code Regs. 3.16'. The guards ('(Ill. 2020)' N.E.3d, 'section 9 of chapter 93A' without 'General Laws') were confirmed not to route.

sources.title: General Laws of Massachusetts (malegislature.gov)
sources.publisher: The General Court of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts
sources.official_status_evidence: https://malegislature.gov/Laws/GeneralLaws: 'NOTICE: This is NOT the official version of the General Laws of Massachusetts' ... check the Official Edition (printed every two years).
sources.coverage: All chapters of the General Laws (Parts I-V), section by section; amendments passed before May 31, 2026 per landing-page notice.

access.pattern_rules: chapter and section exactly as cited, letters upper-case (93A, 151B; 13A, 60B, 11I); lower-case is accepted (Chapter93a redirects). The short form redirects to the canonical /Laws/GeneralLaws/Part{I-V}/Title{roman}/Chapter{chapter}/Section{section} URL, so Part/Title need not be known (verified: c.93A s.9 -> PartI/TitleXV; c.231 s.85 -> PartIII/TitleII; c.151B s.4 -> PartI/TitleXXI; c.265 s.13A -> PartIV/TitleI; c.12 s.11I -> PartI/TitleII; c.149 s.148 -> PartI/TitleXXI). A non-existent section returns HTTP 404 (Chapter93A/Section99), not a soft page. Chapter page without section: /Laws/GeneralLaws/Chapter{chapter} (redirects to the chapter's section list). A section range '§§ 60B-60E' is a span: fetch the first section, then each one.
access.navigation: Not needed (short URL redirects). If a redirect ever fails: /Laws/GeneralLaws -> Part{I..V} page lists Titles WITH chapter ranges (e.g. 'Title XV ... Chapters 93 - 110H') -> Title page -> Chapter page -> Section link.
